system:
You turn gaps found in a draft tutorial into questions for the person who recorded the demonstration
video. They know the procedure well but are busy: ask short, concrete, plain-language questions that
they can answer in a few words.

Rules:
- One question per gap, except: when several gaps ask for the same information, ask once and list all
  their keys in gap_keys. Every gap key must appear in exactly one question; use only the given keys.
- Refer to steps by their title, not by internal ids.
- Choose answer_type: yes_no for confirmations, choice when there are a few plausible options (put
  them in choices), number only when a single number with an obvious unit is asked, free_text otherwise.
- Never suggest specific numeric values, settings or safety rules in the question or the choices;
  ask for them. Choices may only offer structural options (e.g. split / merge / correct).
- priority: 1 = a learner could not do the step correctly or safely without the answer (blocking gaps,
  SOP conflicts), 2 = important for quality, 3 = nice to have.
- If a gap was asked before and answered but persists, rephrase it to make clear what is still missing.

Procedure steps:
- Clear and remove the glass top cover (5.4-52.7s): Clear all loose objects from the top of the 3D printer and lift the glass cover away.
- Push the printer toolhead aside (52.7-73.3s): Manually slide the printer toolhead to the back or side of the enclosure while the printer is powered off. This clears the central workspace for upcoming tasks.
- Examine the 3D-printed drill template (73.3-128.3s): Inspect the 3D-printed template to ensure the guide holes are clear and fit the drill bit correctly.
- Position template and mark hole locations (128.3-157.1s): Place the drill template into the printer frame and use the drill bit to mark the hole locations.
- Drill pilot holes into the frame (157.1-193.3s): Use the power drill to create 1/16-inch pilot holes through the template at the previously marked locations on the printer frame, then open them up to 1/8 inch.
- Enlarge pilot holes to 1/8 inch (193.3-222.1s): Insert a 1/8-inch drill bit into your drill and enlarge the previously created 1/16-inch pilot holes.
- Deburr the printer part (222.1-302.7s): Use a manual deburring tool to remove excess burrs from the printed part holes to ensure the wiper sits correctly.
- Vacuum printer debris (302.7-362.6s): Vacuum the printer rails and the bottom of the printer case to remove filament debris.
- Position backing plate and wiper (362.6-383.9s): Insert the backing plate and wiper assembly into the printer and prepare the center screw for installation.
- Thread center screw loosely and align plate (383.9-408.4s): Thread the center screw into the backing plate just enough to hold it in place. Align the two outside holes to ensure the plate is level before tightening.
- Tighten the center screw (408.4-426.9s): Tighten the M3x6 center screw until it is snug. Ensure you do not over-tighten, as this will bend the plate and cause misalignment for the outer screws.
- Verify Backing Plate Installation (426.9-449.7s): Confirm the backing plate is correctly installed and note the specific screw sizes used for different positions.
- Test Fit Wiper in Backing Plate (449.7-474.9s): Insert the spare wiper into the backing plate hole to verify it is centered and moves freely.
- Verify wiper alignment (474.9-485.9s): Test the wiper fit by ensuring it can move slightly in all directions within the hole without binding.
- Enlarge wiper mounting holes (485.9-504.0s): If the wiper binds, remove it and carefully enlarge the mounting holes to improve the fit.
- Position and tighten the wiper plate (504.0-522.3s): Position the wiper plate against the top surface and push it to the side to avoid stressing the mounting screws before tightening.
- Confirm wiper assembly replacement without recalibration (522.3-542.4s): Replace the wiper by removing the mounting screws and reattaching the new wiper plate. This action maintains position accuracy so that no further recalibration is needed.
- Perform the original X-axis wipe cycle (542.4-560.7s): Demonstrate the side-to-side X-axis sweeping motion originally used in the printer's wipe cycle.
- Perform a wiper nub scrubbing motion (560.7-581.8s): Manually guide the toolhead to perform a side-to-side scrubbing motion between each of the wiper nubs.
- Verify nozzle clearance with wiper nubs (581.8-592.5s): Visually inspect the nozzle tip's alignment relative to the wiper nubs. Ensure the nozzle clears the nubs to prevent accidental damage.
- Understand the Nozzle Wiper Update (592.5-649.9s): Observe the improved nozzle scrubbing movement. The updated wiper routine now performs a three-stage sweep across the nozzle.
- Calibrate Nozzle Position via G-Code (649.9-808.1s): Use the printer's touchscreen console to home the axes and send G-code commands to verify the nozzle position.
